title: SLO Trigger Lifecycle Optimizer for Canary Rollbacks
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Implement an automated, tunable rollback trigger service that combines latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput signals to decide safe canary rollbacks. The system must support per-route and per-cohort baselines, traffic-aware hysteresis, cost-normalized thresholds, and human-in-loop approvals. Scope includes a lightweight decision engine, integration with the Redwood Console for visualization and runbooks, synthetic probe tie-ins, and an opt-in safety mode for Dedicated/Private customers. Out of scope: model training or automatic model retraining; out-of-band billing changes.
background: We've seen multiple incidents where single-signal triggers (p95 latency or error rate) either (a) fired on noise during traffic spikes or (b) failed to catch cost regressions that manifest as token inflation. Prior tickets implemented single-metric heuristics; this ticket builds a multi-signal lifecycle optimizer that reduces false positives, increases signal explainability, and normalizes cost signals to avoid unnecessary rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Canary rollback decisions can be made automatically when configured and documented in Console with a rollback reason that references the contributing signals
False positive rate for automated rollbacks reduces by >40% on historical canaries (A/B test window) compared to current fixed-threshold triggers
Operators can set per-route/cohort baselines and a global safety cooldown; default config is conservative for hosted customers
Rollback actions are auditable in the deployment timeline with links to the decision score and contributing metrics
Service supports a manual override and a staged rollback (fractional traffic evacuation) option
design_decisions: Signal fusion: use weighted z-score fusion instead of naive threshold AND/OR to combine latency, error rate, throughput dip, and token-cost drift
Baselineing: maintain rolling cohort baselines per route (7-day rolling median) and a short-term volatility estimate to avoid reacting to transient spikes
Detection algorithms: primary detector = Bayesian change-point for token-cost and throughput; secondary detectors = EWMA-based drift for latency and binomial test for error rate
Traffic-aware hysteresis: require metric exceedance on three consecutive evaluation windows or N% of request cohorts before action
Cost normalization: convert token-cost changes into an expected latency/capacity impact score so cost-only regressions are weighted according to business impact
Explainability: produce a human-readable decision summary that lists top-3 contributing signals and their relative weights
Safety defaults: opt-in automated rollback for Dedicated/Private; hosted defaults to conservative alert-only mode for first 90 days
Cooldown and backoff: after any automated rollback, enforce a 30m cooldown and exponential backoff before another auto-action
tradeoffs: Complex fusion reduces false positives but increases model complexity and initial tuning effort
Per-route baselines improve precision but increase storage and compute for baseline maintenance
Strong hysteresis prevents oscillation but can delay remediation for real regressions; we mitigate with synthetic probes and severity weighting
Cost-normalization requires business-defined cost-to-impact mappings; we provide sensible defaults but allow customer overrides
implementation_plan: Spike (1 week): implement a simulator that replays historical canary traffic and runs candidate detectors against stored metrics
Engine (2 wks): implement a lightweight decision engine in Go with plugin detectors and a small policy DSL for weights and hysteresis
Console UI (2 wks parallel): add Config screen to Redwood Console for per-route policy and an Audit timeline view showing decision breakdowns
Integration (1 wk): wire decision engine into rollout controller to execute staged rollbacks and emit events to activity log
Testing (2 wks): run canary simulation suite, A/B test against existing threshold-based triggers, and runbook validation
Rollout (gradual): start with internal alpha, then opt-in beta customers, then default conservative mode for hosted after 90 days
testing_plan: Unit tests for each detector and fusion function
Simulator-based regression tests using 12 months of canary data and randomized noise injections
A/B experiment: compare control (current threshold triggers) vs treatment (fusion engine) on historical buckets for FP/FN rates
Chaos tests: inject synthetic latency and token inflation into staging canaries and verify hysteresis and cooldown behavior
Load tests: ensure decision engine latency < 200ms at 5000 canaries/sec evaluation rate
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal alpha (team only) — validate decisions on internal canaries and runbook accuracy
Phase 1: Beta — opt-in customers for Dedicated and Private; collect feedback and tune defaults
Phase 2: Hosted alert-only defaults — surface decisions as recommendations in Console for 90 days
Phase 3: Gradual enablement — expose automated rollback toggle per workspace; default remains off for new tenants until maturity metrics met
Emergency escape: manual global kill-switch in Console for operator-initiated disable
